editorial_candidates.excerpt: The example lists the coordinate root sets and standard simple roots, then says each has its standard Dynkin diagram, but shows no diagram.
editorial_candidates.rationale: A compact diagram would connect the four coordinate families to the standard classification and make the B/C double edge and D fork visible. The source supplies the root families and simple-root labels, so this can be added without inventing root data.
editorial_candidates.diagram_content: Draw indexed families A_{n-1}, B_n, C_n, D_n. Label nodes by the simple roots from line 44; use the standard chain for A, the terminal double bond and orientation for B/C, and the terminal fork for D_n. Treat the separately stated D_2 pair as two disconnected A_1 nodes.
